question: In a proportional high-dimensional model of in-context linear-regression weight prediction, how do finite pretraining-task diversity, inference context length, label noise, and the number of repeated learned updates jointly determine whether more test-time chain-of-thought steps reduce error exponentially or polynomially, saturate, or amplify error?

key_findings.claim: The paper operationalizes chain of thought as repeated application of one learned preconditioned-gradient update, rather than as semantic or token-level reasoning.
key_findings.evidence: A restricted one-layer linear-attention model learns only a matrix A. Its readout equals the current weight estimate minus D times A times the empirical squared-loss gradient, and the noiseless test error follows the linear recursion w minus w-hat_t = (I minus A S divided by alpha)^t w.

anchors.section: 3 / Simplified parameterization and CoT in inference phase

key_findings.claim: Finite-depth mean-squared error is reduced to derivatives of a two-variable resolvent and, in the ridgeless proportional limit, to an explicit scalar generating function.
key_findings.evidence: The error is a finite binomial combination of mixed moments of A S and S A-transpose. A 4D-by-4D block linearization removes the inverse inside the learned A, and leave-one-sample/task cavity equations close the normalized block traces; for lambda zero the mixed trace m13 is solved in terms of one Wishart resolvent g.

key_findings.claim: The advertised ridgeless closed form is not defined for the full positive task-diversity range stated around Result 1.
key_findings.evidence: At lambda zero, C is a sum of M rank-one outer products and is singular whenever M<D, while A-star is written as B C-inverse. The explicit solution also contains repeated factors of 1/(tau-1). Result 1 does not state tau>1; that restriction appears only in Result 2, so the lambda-zero formula cannot cover tau less than or equal to one without a pseudoinverse or limiting-ridge prescription that the paper does not give.

key_findings.claim: The manuscript's repeated description of the asymptotic formula as exact overstates the proof status.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix explicitly says the derivation is not fully rigorous and relies on unproved self-averaging, leave-one-out replacements, and deterministic-equivalent substitutions. Numerical agreement supports the result but does not turn those steps into a theorem.

key_findings.claim: Under the ridgeless asymptotic analysis with task-diversity ratio tau greater than one, a critical tau_c separates error amplification from stable refinement, and context ratio alpha separates zero-error decay from an information-limited floor.
key_findings.evidence: Result 2 gives E_t minus E_infinity asymptotic to K t^{-1/2} Lambda^t. Lambda is above, at, or below one as tau lies below, at, or above tau_c; when alpha is below one and tau is sufficiently large, E_infinity remains positive, while otherwise the stated limit is zero.

key_findings.claim: The long-depth phase boundary is conditional on an unproved multivariate singularity assumption, and the optimal-depth law adds a transversality assumption.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix F assumes that the symmetric critical point is the unique dominant singularity and that no smaller-modulus singularity contributes. Appendix H further assumes this point crosses the unit circle transversely so log Lambda is linear in tau_c minus tau. These are essential to the t^{-1/2} Lambda^t and t-star scaling claims.

key_findings.claim: Appendix F does not derive all of Result 2 despite being presented as its detailed derivation.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix restates the limiting floor and rate, then analyzes a denominator zero after introducing an undefined E-new quantity. It assumes a symmetric dominant point, obtains its unit-circle crossing, and solves for tau_c. It never derives the displayed E_infinity formula, proves which side of the crossing has Lambda above or below one, or excludes the branch loci and explicit (1-x)(1-y) poles from dominance.

anchors.section: F / Assumed smooth symmetric point and Equations 292-296
F / Unit-circle crossing and tau_c calculation

key_findings.claim: In the favorable population-risk and context-rich limit, the test error has an exponential factor whose rate improves with context length, multiplied by a t^{-3/2} spectral-edge correction.
key_findings.evidence: For tau tending to infinity, lambda zero, and alpha greater than one, Theorem 3 obtains E_t asymptotic up to constants to t^{-3/2} times ((2 square-root alpha plus sigma-squared)/(alpha plus 1 plus sigma-squared))^{2t}; when alpha dominates noise this becomes t^{-3/2}(4/alpha)^t.

key_findings.claim: Theorem 3's printed Marchenko-Pastur integral has a normalization error, although that error does not change its depth exponent or exponential rate.
key_findings.evidence: For S=XX-transpose with L/D=alpha>1, the D-normalized spectrum on [(1-sqrt(alpha))^2,(1+sqrt(alpha))^2] has continuous density sqrt((s_plus-s)(s-s_minus))/(2 pi s). The appendix prints an extra 1/alpha and simultaneously says there is no zero atom; that density integrates to 1/alpha, so Equation 311 would give E_0=1/alpha instead of the model's E_0=1. Multiplying the measure by alpha repairs normalization and leaves the t^{-3/2} r_alpha^{2t} equivalence unchanged up to constants.

key_findings.claim: Near the overthinking boundary from below, the proposed optimal stopping depth diverges inversely with the task-diversity gap and its best error falls only as the inverse square root of that depth.
key_findings.evidence: Under the smooth transverse-crossing assumption, minimizing the continuous proxy t^{-1/2} exp(kappa (tau_c minus tau)t) gives t-star proportional to 1/(tau_c minus tau) and E_{t-star} proportional to t-star^{-1/2}. The appendix does not supply a uniform two-parameter remainder that would transfer this proxy minimizer to the exact discrete MSE, so this is a conditional formal scaling law rather than a proved argmin theorem.

key_findings.claim: The asymptotic label 'stable refinement' does not establish monotone improvement at every finite depth.
key_findings.evidence: Result 2 controls only the large-t diagonal coefficient through Lambda and a limiting floor. The learned propagator A-star S is generally non-symmetric, and no contraction, normality, or finite-t sign argument is proved. Thus Lambda below one implies eventual damping under the stated singularity assumptions, not the main-text assertion that increasing depth consistently reduces error throughout the trajectory.

key_findings.claim: The saturation floor is a test-information limitation in this Gaussian regression model: when the context has fewer examples than dimensions, no number of stable iterations can identify unseen weight components.
key_findings.evidence: For alpha below one, Result 2 gives a nonzero E_infinity in the stable regime. Section 5.3 attributes it to rank-deficient test covariance, so adding update steps cannot recover directions absent from the prompt.

key_findings.claim: Finite-dimensional experiments support the simplified model's phase taxonomy, but discrepancies grow with reasoning depth and the paper reports only leading-order convergence rather than a finite-size correction.
key_findings.evidence: Across selected saturation, overthinking, polynomial, and exponential settings, five-trial curves approach the asymptotic prediction as D increases. At longer depth the empirical MSE is systematically larger, with the gap attributed to omitted finite-size effects.

key_findings.claim: Fully learned linear and softmax attention reproduce the three broad behaviors qualitatively, but they do not validate the exact threshold, asymptotic exponents, or softmax exponential rate.
key_findings.evidence: At D=50 and depth 20, five-trial M-by-L phase diagrams show decay, overthinking, and saturation. The text says the linear model is close to exponential while the softmax decrease is more gradual, and describes the agreement only as qualitative.

key_findings.claim: The claim that inference computation is proportional to reasoning depth is inaccurate for the implemented full-history prompt.
key_findings.evidence: The main text states computation is proportional to t, but every step appends an estimate token and lets the final query attend to all L examples and all previous estimates. Even when only the final token is updated, summing source-token work over steps scales as O(tL+t^2), not O(t).

key_findings.claim: The experimental extension changes several theoretically material conditions at once, so its transfer evidence does not isolate attention nonlinearity.
key_findings.evidence: Theory uses Gaussian inputs scaled by 1/D, zero initialization, optional pretraining label noise, and the restricted matrix A. The extension uses unscaled Gaussian inputs and weights, random initial estimates, noiseless tasks, full query/key/value matrices, a full-history mask, and Adam training. Those changes prevent attributing departures solely to linear versus softmax attention.

key_findings.claim: The empirical defense of the fixed sparse block parameterization is suggestive but not quantitative.
key_findings.evidence: Two learned-matrix heatmaps at small and larger task/example counts visually show the intended routing blocks emerging and other blocks staying small, but no block-norm error, prediction equivalence, seed uncertainty, or downstream phase comparison between restricted and unrestricted models is reported.

method.core_idea: Learn a matrix-valued preconditioner from finitely many Gaussian linear-regression tasks, reuse it recurrently on a fresh prompt, and solve the resulting nonnormal random linear iteration in the proportional D,L,M limit through a two-point resolvent.
method.mechanism: The restricted attention block produces a preconditioned empirical-gradient update. Ridge empirical-risk minimization gives A-star=B C-inverse from M task statistics. At inference the fixed A-star composes with an independent Wishart covariance S for t steps. A bivariate generating function encodes every mixed moment needed for the MSE; a block linearization plus inference-sample and pretraining-task cavity equations produces deterministic trace equations, which are solved explicitly at zero ridge. Multivariate coefficient asymptotics then locate the claimed task-diversity transition and Marchenko-Pastur edge analysis gives the favorable-regime rate. Finite-D simulations and fully learned linear/softmax attention test qualitative transfer.
assumptions: Inputs and task weights are isotropic Gaussian, pretraining tasks share one context length and noise level, and test labels are noiseless.
Dimension D, context length L, and number of pretraining tasks M diverge proportionally with fixed positive alpha=L/D and tau=M/D.
The main closed form and phase analysis use the ridgeless lambda=0 solution, with figures using lambda=10^-5 as a numerical proxy.
The lambda=0 inverse and displayed closed form require tau>1; no pseudoinverse continuation is defined for tau less than or equal to one.
A strong sparse block structure is fixed so only the D-by-D update matrix A is learned in the solvable model.
Cavity quadratic forms self-average and leave-one-out resolvents may be replaced by deterministic equivalents; the appendix does not prove these steps.
The symmetric singular point is the unique dominant point for diagonal coefficient asymptotics, with no closer branch or pole contribution.
The critical point crosses the unit circle transversely when deriving the optimal-depth divergence.
Qualitative phases in a one-layer synthetic weight-prediction task are informative about chain-of-thought behavior in language models.

techniques.role: Turns a prompt of labeled Gaussian examples into direct estimation of the latent regression vector, making reasoning error exactly measurable.
Represents each reasoning step as reuse of the same learned empirical-gradient transform.
Keeps task diversity and context scarcity nontrivial as dimension grows.
Encodes mixed moments of the nonnormal forward and transpose error propagators needed for finite-depth MSE.
Embeds the inverse inside the learned update into a 4D block matrix so one resolvent block equals the desired two-point function.
Uses separate leave-one-inference-sample and leave-one-pretraining-task perturbations to close scalar trace order parameters.
Extracts the long-depth exponential factor and polynomial prefactor from diagonal coefficients of the generating function.
Derives the t^{-3/2} correction and favorable-regime rate from the lower spectral edge.
Lets experimental models reuse all generated estimates while preventing the final estimate token from attending to itself.

evaluations.setting: Restricted linear-attention model across representative exponential, polynomial, saturation, and overthinking parameter settings with sigma=0.01, lambda=10^-5, increasing finite D, and five trials
evaluations.metric: Test weight-estimation MSE as a function of reasoning depth
evaluations.result: Finite-D trajectories approach the D-to-infinity prediction as D grows; empirical error exceeds theory increasingly at long depth.
evaluations.baseline: Coefficient-extracted ridgeless asymptotic curve from Result 1

evaluations.setting: Fully learned one-layer linear attention on noiseless D=50 synthetic tasks over an M-by-L grid, evaluated at depth 20 with five trials per point
evaluations.metric: Long-depth MSE phase diagram and MSE-versus-depth trajectories
evaluations.result: Small M produces overthinking; larger M separates context-limited saturation from a decay regime that is close to the predicted exponential shape.
evaluations.baseline: Four-regime phase taxonomy of the restricted high-dimensional model

evaluations.setting: Fully learned one-layer softmax attention on the same D=50 task family, grid, depth, and five-trial protocol
evaluations.metric: Long-depth MSE phase diagram and MSE-versus-depth trajectories
evaluations.result: Decay, saturation, and overthinking all appear qualitatively, but decay over the displayed range is more gradual than the theoretical exponential law.
evaluations.baseline: Matched fully learned linear-attention experiment and restricted-model phase prediction

evaluations.setting: Unrestricted linear-attention parameter matrices at two reported small/larger task-and-example settings
evaluations.metric: Visual heatmaps of learned W and V block structure
evaluations.result: The intended routing and update blocks become visually prominent while other blocks appear small, especially with more data.
evaluations.baseline: Fixed sparse block parameterization used by the solvable model

evaluations.setting: Each trained experimental model evaluated on 4,096 independently sampled noiseless test tasks after 3,000 Adam steps at learning rate 10^-3, batch size 300, and lambda=10^-5
evaluations.metric: Mean parameter MSE with standard error across five training trials
evaluations.result: The reported curves distinguish the three stable/unstable qualitative behaviors but do not estimate tau_c or asymptotic exponents with confidence intervals.
evaluations.baseline: Same architecture at alternative M and L values rather than a non-recurrent or compute-matched reasoning baseline

limitations: Author-stated: the theory is restricted to a linear in-context learner in which chain of thought is iterative weight refinement, not realistic language reasoning.
Author-stated: the appendix derivation is not fully rigorous and leaves self-averaging, leave-one-out, and deterministic-equivalent steps unjustified.
Author-stated: the softmax experiment preserves the qualitative phases but not the precise exponential decay visible in linear attention.
Reviewer-identified: Result 1 presents a lambda=0 closed form without stating tau>1 even though C is rank deficient for M<D and the solution contains 1/(tau-1).
Reviewer-identified: the phase-rate proof assumes a unique dominant symmetric singular point; no exclusion of competing singularities is proved.
Reviewer-identified: Appendix F never derives the stated limiting floor, does not define E-new relative to E-E_infinity, and does not prove the side-of-crossing inequalities for Lambda.
Reviewer-identified: the optimal-depth divergence additionally assumes a smooth transverse crossing and an unspecified positive derivative kappa.
Reviewer-identified: applying the large-t equivalent to the exact discrete argmin also needs uniform control as tau approaches tau_c; no such remainder bound is supplied.

Reviewer-identified: Appendix G's printed Marchenko-Pastur density is smaller by a factor alpha, so its integral representation gives E_0=1/alpha rather than 1; the missing constant does not alter the claimed t-rate.
Reviewer-identified: Result 2 does not restate lambda=0 even though its closed-form derivation uses the ridgeless solution, while phase figures use lambda=10^-5.
Reviewer-identified: Lambda<1 is an eventual asymptotic statement and does not prove the main-text claim of finite-depth monotonic improvement for a generally nonnormal propagator.
Reviewer-identified: the learnable model is reduced to one D-by-D block; two visual heatmaps do not establish quantitative equivalence to full parameter training.
Reviewer-identified: fully learned experiments alter normalization, initialization, masking, parameterization, and noise together, so they do not isolate nonlinear attention as the transfer variable.
Reviewer-identified: all tasks are isotropic Gaussian regression at D=50 for the expressive models; no language, discrete reasoning, distribution shift, or trained LLM is evaluated.
Reviewer-identified: five training trials and qualitative phase labels are insufficient to verify a sharp critical boundary or polynomial/exponential asymptotic exponents.
Reviewer-identified: no direct baseline stops adaptively, uses a damping schedule, or allocates the same inference FLOPs without recurrent history.
Reviewer-identified: total full-history inference work grows as O(tL+t^2), contradicting the main text's statement that it is proportional to t.
Reviewer-identified: training uses a one-step weight target, so the paper studies recurrent reuse of a direct predictor rather than learning from natural chain-of-thought traces.

Reviewer-identified: the main claim overlaps strongly with arXiv:2510.03605, which already studies the same weight-prediction/test-time iteration and harmful scaling under insufficient training coverage.
failure_modes: Too few pretraining tasks make the learned update operator unstable in some directions, so repeated application eventually amplifies estimation error.
Too few test examples leave a null space in the empirical covariance; stable iterations converge but cannot recover those missing weight components.
Near the critical boundary, a long but finite useful horizon can make a shallow evaluation look monotone even though asymptotic overthinking is predicted.
A ridge value, anisotropic covariance, non-Gaussian task family, or noisy test labels may move or remove the stated phase boundary because the closed result is specialized.
Softmax normalization changes effective step size and can replace the predicted exponential curve with much slower dynamics.
Full-history recurrence incurs quadratic-in-depth source-token work and can be less efficient than a compute-matched fixed-context loop.
A nonnormal learned propagator can exhibit transient growth not summarized by its eventual exponential factor or limiting floor.
Finite-D corrections accumulate with depth, causing the asymptotic curve to underestimate realized error where stopping decisions matter most.
Language-model chain of thought may branch, revise, retrieve, or alter representations rather than reuse one stationary linear update, breaking the model analogy.
reusable_insights: Separate test-time scaling into update quality, information availability, and iteration count; more steps cannot compensate for either an unstable update or missing observations.
For learned recurrent inference, analyze mixed forward/transpose moments rather than only eigenvalues when the update operator is nonnormal.
A finite optimal depth can diverge near a stability boundary, so stopping policies should be estimated jointly with training-data coverage rather than fixed globally.
Report both the convergence rate and the asymptotic floor: two systems can have faster early decay but worse long-horizon information limits.
Validate asymptotic reasoning laws with dimension sweeps and explicitly measure the depth at which finite-size error departs from theory.
Count accumulated inference FLOPs for growing scratchpads or histories; reasoning-step count alone is not a compute measure.
When claiming transfer from a solvable model, vary one departure at a time—parameter freedom, normalization, softmax, initialization, noise, and history.
open_questions: Can the cavity equations and bivariate coefficient asymptotics be made rigorous, including proof of the dominant critical point and its transverse crossing?
How do nonzero ridge, anisotropic or heavy-tailed task covariances, noisy test labels, and pretrain-test mismatch change tau_c and the saturation floor?
Can the limiting-floor formula and side-of-boundary inequalities in Result 2 be derived while accounting for resolvent branch loci and the explicit coefficient-extraction poles?
Does a fixed-size recurrent state show the same phase diagram when inference FLOPs, rather than generated-step count, are matched?
Can an observable stability statistic predict the optimal stopping depth on a new task without knowing tau or the ground-truth error?
Which phase features survive in multi-layer transformers trained on natural reasoning traces rather than direct synthetic weight targets?
Can nonnormal transient amplification create useful-then-harmful behavior even when the asymptotic spectral radius is stable?
How does learned damping, momentum, adaptive step size, or step-dependent attention alter the four regimes?
Can the sharp boundary be statistically located with finite D and uncertainty rather than assigned by visual phase labels?

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding the Role of Training Data in Test-Time Scaling
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest direct predecessor using the same in-context weight-prediction task, direct training, and repeated test-time updates.
competitive_landscape.difference: Javanmard et al. characterize a learned pseudo-Newton iteration under general feature covariance and already show that missing training directions make more test-time compute harmful. This paper instead keeps isotropic tasks but makes the number of pretraining tasks finite and proportional to dimension, derives a two-point random-matrix formula, and divides the M-by-L plane into exponential, polynomial, saturation, and overthinking regimes.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers Learn to Implement Multi-step Gradient Descent with Chain of Thought
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct task and mechanism prior for chain-of-thought weight prediction.
competitive_landscape.difference: Huang et al. analyze training on autoregressive intermediate weight targets and prove that the learned transformer executes multi-step gradient descent with near-exact recovery. The present model trains a one-step direct predictor and studies finite-task statistical error when that stationary update is reused only at test time.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v1 (2025-02-28; current on 2026-08-23); ICLR 2025 Spotlight

competitive_landscape.title: Asymptotic Theory of In-Context Learning by Linear Attention
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational asymptotic linear-attention ICL prior from the same research line.
competitive_landscape.difference: Lu et al. derive sharp proportional-limit learning curves, double descent, and a memorization-to-ICL phase transition for direct prediction as pretraining examples, context, and task diversity scale. This paper adds recurrent test-time application of the learned operator and analyzes error as a function of reasoning depth.

competitive_landscape.title: Theory of Scaling Laws for In-Context Regression: Depth, Width, Context and Time
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest asymptotic scaling-law work on depth and context in linear self-attention.
competitive_landscape.difference: Bordelon et al. vary trained model depth, width, optimization time, and task covariance structure and derive compute-optimal ICL scaling. The present paper holds architecture to one recurrently reused layer, makes inference-step depth the variable, and focuses on stability, saturation, and optimal stopping from finite task diversity.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v1 (2025-10-01; current on 2026-08-23); ICLR 2026 conference paper

competitive_landscape.title: How does Chain of Thought decompose complex tasks?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Concurrent theory of when deeper chain-of-thought helps, saturates, or has an optimal finite depth.
competitive_landscape.difference: Nadgir et al. model reasoning as a tree of smaller classification problems and derive a critical branching degree and optimal depth from class-count power laws. This paper models a learned linear iterative estimator and locates phases through pretraining-task and context ratios using random matrix theory.

competitive_landscape.title: Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Adjacent theory linking pretraining data quality to later reasoning improvement.
competitive_landscape.difference: Javanmard et al. analyze how balanced pretraining creates latent capabilities and how SFT versus RL data difficulty activates them, with nonlinear-transformer experiments. The present work isolates repeated inference-time updates without SFT or RL and derives a task-count/context phase diagram.

competitive_landscape.title: Loop, Think, & Generalize: Implicit Reasoning in Recurrent-Depth Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current recurrent-depth competitor that directly documents useful depth extrapolation and overthinking in transformer reasoning.
competitive_landscape.difference: Kohli et al. train recurrent-depth transformers on controlled multi-hop composition and empirically show both extrapolation beyond training depth and degradation under excessive recurrence. The present paper supplies a solvable linear-regression phase diagram and task/context scaling law, but its transfer experiment is much smaller and does not test compositional reasoning.

competitive_landscape.title: Stabilizing Recurrent Dynamics for Test-Time Scalable Latent Reasoning in Looped Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest current stability-focused competitor for recurrent test-time scaling and collapse after an optimal loop depth.
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. analyze looped-language-model latent dynamics and regularize the Jacobian spectral radius to approach stable fixed points, with arithmetic and mathematical-reasoning experiments. The present paper predicts instability from finite pretraining-task diversity in a fixed Gaussian estimator but proposes no stability intervention or language-model test.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first exact high-dimensional characterization that unifies exponential and polynomial improvement, saturation, and overthinking as functions of chain-of-thought depth, pretraining task diversity, and context length, including an optimal-depth scaling law and validation in fully learned linear and softmax attention.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The new technical object is a two-point generating function for a learned, generally non-symmetric update composed with an independent inference covariance; its ridgeless solution yields a joint alpha-tau phase diagram and depth asymptotics.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest incremental novelty is the finite-pretraining-task proportional random-matrix treatment: a two-point finite-depth MSE representation, a joint task-diversity/context phase proposal with an information floor, and a formal near-boundary stopping law. The broad mechanism and harmful-scaling claim are not new—arXiv:2510.03605v2 studies the same direct-trained weight predictor and repeated test-time pseudo-Newton updates, arXiv:2502.21212v1 establishes multi-step gradient descent in this CoT task, and arXiv:2604.07822v2 plus arXiv:2605.26733v1 directly study recurrent-depth overthinking and stability. The paper is therefore a sharper asymptotic specialization, not a first general theory of CoT. Even within that specialization, 'exact' is too strong: the cavity closure is acknowledged non-rigorous, the lambda-zero formula omits its tau>1 domain, the phase proof assumes rather than proves dominance and omits the floor derivation, the optimal-depth argmin lacks uniform error control, and Appendix G misnormalizes its spectral measure. The external evidence remains qualitative synthetic transfer.

reviewer_notes: Independent second pass over the exact 47-page arXiv:2606.03217v1 artifact. The local PDF SHA-256 was streamed against the versioned arXiv PDF and matched b713fd487dfaddeaf892f7e4767d9fefd8be9e47736ee5c233c3516e6a1944c4. I rechecked the model/readout (pages 3-5 and 15-20), all cavity sectors and their closure (pages 21-37), coefficient recursion and finite-D plots (pages 37-39), the full singularity calculation (pages 39-42), the Marchenko-Pastur and stopping arguments (pages 43-45), and the complete expressive-model protocol (pages 46-47). The newly recorded tau-domain omission, missing floor proof, nonuniform argmin step, and Marchenko-Pastur normalization error were found independently and were not rubber-stamped from the first pass. The O(tL+t^2) statement is arithmetic from the explicit growing source-token count, not a measured runtime. Code was not executed, so verified denotes passage/provenance/competitor verification rather than experimental reproduction.
